Any authenticated user (including tenants and workers) can scan user IDs and distinguish existing users from non-existing ones, enabling targeted credential-stuffing or phishing attacks.

extra.message: CSV formula injection via unit number in inspections export

metadata.proof: The inspections export writes i.unit.unit_number into a CSV cell without formula sanitization. Unit.unit_number is user-supplied (String(40), set by managers/admins via /api/units or CSV import). A manager can assign a formula payload such as '=HYPERLINK("http://evil.com")' to a unit number, which executes when another admin/manager opens inspections.csv.

extra.message: Unbounded maintenance export can exhaust server memory

metadata.proof: export_maintenance uses .all() with no LIMIT or pagination. An authenticated admin/manager can trigger an unbounded fetch of all maintenance tickets and joined units, building the entire CSV in memory before responding. With sufficient records, this leads to memory exhaustion and denial of service.

extra.message: Unbounded inspections export can exhaust server memory

metadata.proof: export_inspections calls .all() with no LIMIT or pagination. An authenticated admin/manager can request an export that buffers every inspection record and joined unit into memory, causing unbounded memory/CPU consumption and potential denial of service.

extra.message: Unbounded payments export can exhaust server memory

metadata.proof: export_payments uses .all() with no LIMIT or pagination. An authenticated admin/manager can force the server to load every payment with joined lease and unit into memory to build the CSV, resulting in unbounded resource consumption and denial of service.

extra.message: API keys have no expiration date

metadata.proof: The ApiKey model has created_at and last_used_at but no expires_at column. Keys created via /api/api-keys are valid indefinitely unless manually revoked. A leaked, forgotten, or compromised API key grants indefinite access to the account, violating token-lifecycle best practices (CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration).

extra.message: Password reset revokes sessions but not API keys

metadata.citation:
for s in user.sessions:
        s.revoked = True
metadata.proof: POST /api/auth/password-reset/complete revokes the user's sessions after a password reset but does not revoke their ApiKey rows. An attacker who obtained an API key before the reset can continue to authenticate and act as the user indefinitely after the password reset completes.

extra.message: Disabling a user via admin update revokes sessions but not API keys

metadata.citation:
for s in target.sessions:
                s.revoked = True
metadata.proof: PUT /api/users/{user_id} sets is_active=False and revokes the target's sessions (line 106), but it never revokes the target's ApiKey rows. A disabled user — or anyone holding their API key — can continue to call the API using the key, bypassing the account disablement.

extra.message: Deactivating a user via admin delete revokes sessions but not API keys

metadata.citation:
for s in target.sessions:
                s.revoked = True
metadata.proof: DELETE /api/users/{user_id} deactivates the target and revokes their sessions (line 135), yet leaves their ApiKey rows active. The deactivated user or a key thief retains API access, undermining the account-disable control.

extra.message: Account lockout bypassed by existing sessions and API keys

metadata.proof: Both _user_from_session (line 19) and _user_from_api_key (line 37) authenticate the user by checking only is_active. They never check user.locked_until. When auth.py's login endpoint (routes/auth.py:91) sets locked_until after LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD failed attempts, any pre-existing session cookie or API key continues to authenticate the user, defeating the lockout. An attacker who has obtained a session cookie (e.g., via session fixation or shared machine) can bypass lockout and maintain access.

extra.message: Uploaded sensitive documents stored on disk without encryption

metadata.proof: save_upload (files.py:59) writes uploaded documents—lease agreements, receipts, identity documents, inspection photos—to the uploads directory using plain file I/O with no encryption. The Document model stores only a storage_key path. If the server filesystem is compromised, backed up insecurely, or exposed via container breakout, all sensitive documents are available in cleartext. Application-layer encryption-at-rest is absent.
